reviews.rationale: Selected SEC exhibit rows show a sequentially stronger GAAP revenue and profit picture alongside a modestly lower company-reported effective fee rate excluding performance fees and continued net cash outflows from AUM. The revenue increase is concentrated in investment advisory fees and a swing in capital allocation-based income, while administrative and other fees declined slightly and performance-based advisory fees were flat. Because the selected rows are displayed-value arithmetic only, the split between fee-rate, asset-level and market effects on advisory fees is not established, and the capital allocation swing is not explained by any selected driver. The company-defined adjusted parent net income moved in the same direction as GAAP parent net income but by a smaller amount, so the gap between the two bases is unresolved in this extract. AUM rose with market appreciation smaller than in the prior quarter and outflows still negative, so organic flow direction remains a material counterweight to the profit improvement. The Q3-only model delivery figure has no comparator and is not a net flow, so it cannot be used to offset the outflow evidence. No causal attribution is asserted; the research state is held for review pending fuller filing evidence on fee-rate drivers, the capital allocation swing, and the GAAP-to-adjusted reconciliation.
